body_text: Breakthrough T1D Awards Grant to Support PRISE‑hATG Study of SAB‑142 in Stage 3 Type 1 Diabetes Jul 07, 2026 PDF Version MIAMI, July 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Breakthrough T1D, the leading global type 1 diabetes (T1D) research and advocacy organization and SAB Biotherapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: SABS ), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing a fully human anti-thymocyte immunoglobulin (hATG) for T1D and other autoimmune diseases, today announced that Breakthrough T1D has awarded a grant to Michael J. Haller, M.D., Professor and Chief of Pediatric Endocrinology at the University of Florida in support of PRISE-hATG, a clinical study evaluating SAB-142 in patients with Stage 3 T1D who are 100 days to 2 years from diagnosis. Stage 3 T1D is diagnosed when the disease has progressed to a point where insulin is required. The PRISE-hATG study is designed to assess whether SAB-142 can preserve endogenous C-peptide and modulate immune responses in individuals with residual beta cell function beyond the first 100 days after a Stage 3 diagnosis. It extends SAB BIO’s clinical evaluation of SAB-142 and complements the ongoing Phase 2b SAFEGUARD trial evaluating SAB‑142 in patients with new onset Stage 3 T1D. SAB BIO will co-fund this study. “There is an urgent need for novel disease-modifying therapies for people living with T1D beyond 100 days from a Stage 3 diagnosis who still retain meaningful beta cell function.” said Michael Haller, M.D. , Professor and Chief of Pediatric Endocrinology at the University of Florida and Principal Investigator of PRISE-hATG . “The PRISE-hATG study is designed to evaluate whether immunomodulation with SAB-142 helps preserve insulin-producing beta cells beyond the earliest stages of disease, where all other investigational immunotherapies focused. This study has the potential to meaningfully expand options for the millions of people living with T1D.” “Accelerating the development of new therapies that can change the course of type 1 diabetes is a key priority for Breakthrough T1D,” said Josh Vieth, Ph.D., Senior Director of Research at Breakthrough T1D . “Clinical trials typically focus on the first 100 days after a Stage 3 type 1 diabetes diagnosis, and there remains a need to advance disease-modifying therapies that may benefit individuals who don’t fit this criteria. Determining whether SAB-142 can preserve beta cell function beyond the 100-day window addresses this need and has the potential to expand therapeutic options that can improve the lives of those living with type 1 diabetes. We’re excited to work with Dr. Haller and collaborate with SAB BIO to support this trial.” “PRISE-hATG represents an important extension of our clinical program and reinforces our belief that SAB-142 has the potential to be a best-in-class, disease-modifying therapy for T1D” said Samuel J. Reich, Chief Executive Officer of SAB BIO . “We are grateful to Breakthrough T1D for supporting this research and to Dr. Haller and his team for advancing this important work for patients.” About SAB-142 SAB-142 is a potentially disease-modifying, redosable immunotherapy in clinical development for the treatment of autoimmune type 1 diabetes (T1D). SAB-142 is a multi-specific, fully human anti-thymocyte globulin (hATG) with a mechanism of action analogous to that of rabbit ATG (rATG). rATG has demonstrated in multiple clinical trials the ability to slow disease progression in patients with new- or recent-onset of Stage 3 T1D. SAB-142, like rATG, directly targets multiple immune cells involved in destroying pancreatic beta cells, including modulation of “bad acting” T-lymphocytes. By stopping immune cells from attacking beta cells, this treatment has the potential to preserve insulin-producing beta cells. About PRISE-hATG P ersonalized R esponse and I mmunologic S urveillance of E ndogenous C-Peptide Preservation in New, Recent, and Extended New Onset T1D Treated with h uman A nti- T hymocyte G lobulin is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled investigator-led study. This study is designed to assess the safety, efficacy, and tolerability of SAB-142 in individuals in an extended time period after diagnosis (>100 days to 1 year, and 1 year to 2 years). Sampling procedures and analytical methods are fully harmonized with the Phase 2b SAFEGUARD trial, enabling cross-cohort comparisons. About SAB BIO SAB BIO is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing multi-specific, high-potency, human immunoglobulin G (hIgG) to treat and prevent immune and autoimmune disorders. Using advanced genetic engineering and antibody science, SAB BIO developed a proprietary technology which holds the potential to generate additional novel therapeutic candidates utilizing the human immune response, without the need for human donors or convalescent plasma. SAB BIO has optimized genetic engineering in the development of transchromosomic cattle, or Tc-Bovine, to produce hIgG. SAB BIO’s drug development production system is able to generate a diverse repertoire of specifically targeted, high-potency, hIgGs that can address a wide range of serious unmet needs in human diseases. The Company’s lead candidate, SAB-142, targets autoimmune T1D with a disease-modifying therapeutic approach that aims to change the T1D treatment paradigm by delaying onset and potentially preventing disease progression of Stage 3 T1D patients. SAB-142 is currently being evaluated in newly diagnosed Stage 3 autoimmune T1D patients in a registrational Phase 2b clinical trial called SAFEGUARD. For more information, visit www.sab.bio . Additional details about SAFEGUARD are available at https://safeguardstudy.com/ . About Breakthrough T1D, Formerly JDRF As the leading global type 1 diabetes research and advocacy organization, Breakthrough T1D helps make everyday life with type 1 diabetes better while driving toward cures. We do this by investing in the most promising research, advocating for progress by working with government to address issues that impact the T1D community, and helping educate and empower individuals facing this condition. title: EXL Digital Audit Solutions
summary: Intelligent workflow for reduced cost and increased compliance in controlled substance record-keeping at retail pharmacies
body_text: How EXL’s Digital Audit Solution works Database preparation It starts with the stacks of binders you now store on premise, containing the documents the DEA requires you to hold for two years. Our team scans these forms and uploads the digitized PDFs, along with associated metadata, into the cloud for easy search and access. A smart engine then scans the database to identify errors and outliers for exception management; clean forms are automatically moved into storage. Both intelligent character recognition (ICR) and optical character recognition (OCR) are utilized to extract text, thereby enhancing the metadata. The cost of doing business? Under the Controlled Substances Act (CSA), the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) requires registered pharmacies to keep and maintain a complete and accurate log of all controlled substances received and dispatched at their locations for a minimum of two years. These records are often manually prepared and maintained. The process can be time-consuming, error-prone, and expensive. Fines and penalties for non-compliance are significant, not to mention the cost in brand reputation for pharmacies that do not pass a DEA audit. For this reason, retail pharmacy firms regularly conduct internal audits to protect against non-compliance. However, the cost of hiring and sending third-party auditors to physical locations, only to sample 5-10% of total documents, is grossly inefficient and ineffective. There must be a better way. Automate to save on 100% total coverage EXL’s digital auditing solution is an intelligent, cloud-based offering that digitizes audit workflows for quick, efficient, and total audit coverage from any remote, browser-based location. It has already been proven to reduce the cost of internal audits by 80% in one large pharma chain, while also providing 100% coverage of stored CSA-related documents. Why spend more time and money sending auditors into the field, in exchange for so little assurance that your records might pass inspection? Take a closer look at EXL’s digital audit solutions. The auditing process When an audit begins, the system uses business rules that you create to extract forms for presentation to your auditor. The auditor reviews each form presented on their personal dashboard to determine whether the form is compliant or not. As decisions are made, the information is compiled and stored in a bespoke report for shared review. These functionalities allow auditors to audit every form easily, leading to a clear-cut compliance report managers can use to enhance compliance. Streamline your audit workflow for lower cost and better governance If you run a retail pharmacy, you will be audited by the DEA. Meet them with confidence, knowing your records fully comply. An intuitive, customized dashboard allows auditors to perform their work using any browser-based device. The biggest pharmacies in North America trust EXL’s digital audit solutions to help them stay compliant. You can, too. For a solution demonstration or to learn more, please visit EXLservice.com/contact .

body_text: View All News Aduro and ECOCE Complete Phase 1 Feedstock Mapping, Advance Mexico Plastics Collaboration to HCT Testing 07/16/2026 Download (opens in new window) Selected streams from Mexico’s flexible and multilayer plastic waste, a category estimated at approximately 1.5 million tonnes annually, advance to HCT testing for circular feedstock evaluation LONDON, Ontario, July 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Aduro Clean Technologies Inc . (“Aduro” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: ADUR ) (TSX: ACT ) (FSE: 9D5 ), a clean technology company using the power of chemistry to transform lower-value feedstocks, like waste plastics, heavy bitumen, and renewable oils, into resources for the 21st century, today announced that its collaboration with ECOCE, A.C. (“ ECOCE ”) has advanced to the next phase following completion of Phase 1 feedstock mapping and stream selection. Selected post-consumer flexible plastic packaging streams in Mexico are now moving into a Hydrochemolytic™ Technology (“ HCT ”) test campaign to evaluate their conversion into liquid hydrocarbon products for downstream circular plastics applications. The collaboration, announced in December 2025 , is structured as a phased, data-driven evaluation of flexible plastic packaging collected through recovery systems in Mexico. Phase 1 drew on ECOCE’s ongoing national feedstock mapping program, conducted for its member companies, from which the parties completed the selection of candidate material streams for the next stage of work. Led by ECOCE, the mapping identified multiple post-consumer flexible packaging streams and assessed them for estimated availability, collection routes, physical form, contamination profile, and preparation requirements. The work identified candidate streams with sufficient available volume to support an industrially relevant evaluation and with material characteristics that warrant advancement to HCT testing. Flexible plastic packaging is one of the most difficult material categories to manage within existing recycling systems. These streams can include polyethylene, polypropylene, and multilayer packaging formats, along with inks, adhesives, mixed structures, small formats, and varying levels of contamination. In line with the waste hierarchy, reduction, reuse, and mechanical recycling remain preferred options where they are technically and economically viable. For flexible packaging streams that are not well suited to mechanical or physical recycling, the collaboration is evaluating whether HCT can provide a route to recover hydrocarbon value from these materials and help return them to the plastics value chain. ECOCE has identified flexible plastic packaging as a major and growing material category in Mexico, with available data indicating that approximately 1.5 million tonnes of flexible plastic packaging are generated annually in the country. Phase 1 has built on that market context by mapping candidate flexible and multilayer plastic packaging waste streams, including material categories, collection routes, geographic sourcing, and indicative contamination levels. The materials mapped through Phase 1 include flexible polypropylene packaging, flexible polyethylene packaging, and multilayer flexible packaging, including common post-consumer formats such as snack and cookie wrappers, grocery and bread bags, seed and grain packaging, pet food packaging, cold-cut and dairy packaging, and resealable pouch formats. ECOCE’s work with leading food and beverage companies, representing more than 400 brands, gives the collaboration practical relevance to packaging value-chain priorities and the need for credible circularity options for difficult-to-recycle flexible packaging. The objective is to build an evidence-based understanding of how selected flexible packaging streams can move through a circular value chain: from post-consumer collection and characterization, through feedstock preparation and HCT conversion, to liquid hydrocarbon products for evaluation by petrochemical and polymer value chains. With Phase 1 complete and the next-phase testing program defined, the collaboration now moves into HCT testing of selected material streams. Aduro will begin with lab-scale evaluation to assess how selected Mexican flexible and multilayer plastic waste streams respond to HCT, including processability, product characteristics, yield, residues, contaminant behaviour, and mass balance. As part of this next phase, Adrián Velasco, Director of Flexible Plastic Packaging at ECOCE, will visit Aduro facilities to review the testing pathway, sample requirements, and pilot-scale development program. The visit will help align ECOCE’s knowledge of recovery systems in Mexico with the Company’s technical evaluation process as selected streams move from feedstock mapping into HCT testing. Successful lab-scale results will inform progression to Phase 3 testing on the Next Generation Process (“NGP”) Pilot Plant to support scale-up assessment, customer evaluation, and future commercial analysis. “Phase 1 has moved this collaboration from a market opportunity into a defined technical feedstock program,” said Ofer Vicus, CEO of Aduro. “ECOCE brings practical insight into how flexible packaging moves through Mexican recovery systems, helping us select representative material streams for HCT testing. The next phase will generate the data that matters for scale-up and economics, including processability, product quality, yield, contaminant behaviour, and the potential value of HCT-derived liquids as circular hydrocarbon feedstocks. This is how Aduro advances commercialization: by connecting real materials, downstream requirements, economic validation, and a clear pathway from lab testing to the NGP Pilot Plant.” “Flexible plastic packaging is one of the most important material-management challenges in Mexico,” said Adrián Velasco, Director of Flexible Plastic Packaging at ECOCE. “Through this collaboration, ECOCE is helping connect real recovery-system data with the technical work needed to evaluate circular solutions for these materials. My visit to Aduro facilities as the collaboration moves into HCT testing will allow us to review the testing pathway directly, align on sample requirements, and better understand how selected Mexican flexible packaging streams could be evaluated for return to the plastics value chain.” Results from the next phase will give Aduro and ECOCE the technical and economic evidence to help assess material suitability, product quality, scale-up requirements, and future commercial options for returning difficult-to-recycle flexible packaging to the plastics value chain. About ECOCE ECOCE, A.C. is a non-profit civil association in Mexico created and supported by the food and beverage industry to promote the proper management, collection, and recycling of post-consumer packaging waste. ECOCE brings together leading beverage and food companies, representing more than 400 brands, along with strategic allies working to advance circular economy practices for packaging in Mexico. ECOCE works with industry, government, educational institutions, civil society, and citizens to strengthen recycling culture, support proper separation and recovery of packaging materials, and help direct post-consumer packaging into recycling systems. As ECOCE expands its focus from PET and other established material streams to flexible plastic packaging, it brings practical knowledge of Mexico recovery systems, packaging formats, collection infrastructure, and member-company circularity priorities. For further information, visit www.ecoce.mx . About Aduro Clean Technologies Aduro Clean Technologies is a developer of patented water-based technologies to chemically recycle waste plastics; convert heavy crude and bitumen into lighter, more valuable oil; and transform renewable oils into higher-value fuels or renewable chemicals. The Company’s Hydrochemolytic™ technology relies on water as a critical agent in a chemistry platform that operates at relatively low temperatures and cost, a game-changing approach that converts low-value feedstocks into resources for the 21st century. For further information, visit www.adurocleantech.com . title: What Is an ADT Feed in Healthcare? (July 2026)
summary: What is an ADT feed? Learn how HL7 v2 admission, discharge, and transfer notifications work, CMS requirements, and how ADT data drives care coordination.
body_text: ADT data moves fast and shows up across a range of healthcare workflows, so it's worth understanding exactly how it works. At its core, an ADT feed is a stream of real-time notifications that tells connected systems whenever a patient is admitted, discharged, or transferred. If you're building workflows on top of this data or just trying to make sense of it, here's what you need to know. TLDR: ADT in healthcare tracks patient admissions, discharges, and transfers via real-time HL7 v2 messages sent to billing, care, and admin systems. An ADT feed is a live notification stream, not a database. CMS requires hospitals to make a reasonable effort to send ADT notifications to a patient’s primary care physician and other identified treating clinicians at the time of admission, discharge, or transfer ( 42 CFR § 482.24(d)(5) ). ADT alerts provide limited clinical detail: they typically lack lab results, medication details, or care plans, and offer no historical record. Feed quality also varies widely by hospital and EHR vendor.Metriport's real-time notifications alert care teams the moment an ADT event occurs, and can be paired with a network query to pull the discharge summary and other transition documents into the patient's record. What ADT Means in Healthcare ADT stands for Admission, Discharge, and Transfer. Every time a patient enters a hospital, leaves one, or moves between care settings, an ADT is recorded and broadcast to connected systems. Think of it as the hospital's running log of patient movement. A patient arrives at the emergency department, gets admitted to a med-surg unit, transfers to the ICU, and eventually discharges home. Each step generates an ADT with timestamps, patient demographics, location data, and attending provider details. That event then flows, in real time, to billing systems, care teams, and any external partners subscribed to the feed. These records feed downstream workflows across the health system, including bed management, care coordination, and regulatory reporting, giving staff a shared, up-to-date view of where each patient is and what stage of care they are in. How ADT Events Are Triggered and Transmitted A registration clerk admitting a patient, a nurse transferring them to the ICU, or a discharge planner finalizing paperwork all trigger a discrete HL7 message. That message gets routed through the facility's ADT system. These messages travel over interfaces built on HL7 v2 , a widely deployed legacy messaging standard used by U.S. hospitals. Each message carries a structured payload: patient identifiers, event type codes, timestamps, and location details that downstream systems parse and act on automatically. HL7 v2 vs. FHIR for ADT Messages ADT notifications are almost exclusively sent using HL7 v2. It has been the established clinical messaging standard since the 1980s and is widely used by hospitals to broadcast patient movements to downstream systems such as pharmacy, billing, and HIE networks. FHIR, the federal standard for APIs and patient data access, is capable of representing ADT workflows but its adoption for ADT feeds is still growing. Because most hospital infrastructure is built on HL7 v2, modern systems typically translate traditional HL7 v2 ADT feeds into FHIR formats using middleware. Common ADT Event Types and HL7 Message Codes Each ADT event code is mapped to a discrete clinical trigger, and a handful of message types account for the majority of these event codes. The Most Common ADT Message Types Code Event Trigger A01 Admit/Visit Notification Patient is admitted to inpatient care A02 Transfer a Patient Patient moves to a different unit or bed A03 Discharge/End Visit Patient is discharged or the visit closes A04 Register a Patient Patient registers for an outpatient or ED visit A08 Update Patient Information Demographics or insurance details change A11 Cancel Admit An admission event is reversed A13 Cancel Discharge A discharge event is reversed ‍ The cancel events (A11 and A13) are frequently overlooked but matter for downstream accuracy, since any system acting on an A01 or A03 needs to know if that event is later reversed. ‍ What Data Lives Inside an ADT Feed Each ADT message packages a snapshot of the patient's current state at the moment the event fires. The core fields present in most messages include: Patient demographics: name, date of birth, and gender Visit information: admission and discharge timestamps, visit identifiers, and encounter status Diagnosis: a diagnosis code and description tied to the encounter Patient location: facility name, and for transfers, the source and destination unit or department Attending physician: name and credentials One distinction worth drawing clearly: an ADT feed is a notification stream, not a database. Each message represents a point-in-time event pushed to subscribers as it happens. A static ADT database, by contrast, is a record store built from those accumulated events over time. The feed tells you something just changed; the database tells you the full history of changes. How ADT Systems Improve Hospital Operations Real-time ADT data gives hospitals a clearer picture of patient flow, which directly affects staffing, bed allocation, and discharge planning. When a patient is admitted, transferred, or discharged, that event triggers downstream coordination across nursing, housekeeping, billing, and care management teams. Without timely ADT feeds, these handoffs rely on manual communication that slows response times and creates gaps in care. ADT Feeds and Care Coordination Across Settings When a patient moves between care settings, that transition is one of the highest-risk moments in their care journey. ADT feeds give care coordinators, health plans, digital health services, and post-acute providers real-time visibility into those moments, so follow-up can happen before gaps form. For example, when a patient is discharged from a hospital, a payer receiving that ADT alert can trigger an outreach workflow within hours instead of days. Community health workers, care managers, and primary care teams can all act on the same event simultaneously. ADT Data and Value-Based Care Value-based care models like ACOs and bundled payment arrangements tie reimbursements to outcomes, and ADT data is one of the few real-time signals available to act on. When a patient is admitted to an outside facility, a timely ADT notification gives care managers a window to intervene before a gap in care widens into a costly complication. CMS Requirements for ADT Notifications The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services issued a rule ( 42 CFR § 482.24(d) ) requiring hospitals to send ADT notifications to a patient's primary care provider and other treating clinicians at the time of admission or registration, and immediately prior to or at the time of discharge or transfer. (The obligation falls on the hospital to send these notifications; there is no corresponding requirement that the receiving provider monitor or act on them.) Hospitals that fail to meet this requirement risk losing Medicare and Medicaid participation. The rule applies to most Medicare-participating hospitals, pushing health systems to invest in reliable ADT data infrastructure to stay compliant. For a detailed breakdown, see the CMS ADT notification requirements FAQ . Limitations and Challenges of ADT Data ADT feeds have real constraints that teams should account for before building workflows around them. ADT data is administrative by design: it typically excludes vitals, imaging results, physician notes, and problem/allergy lists, the clinical context needed to understand what actually happened during the visit. Feed quality varies by hospital and EHR vendor, meaning missing fields, inconsistent formatting, and duplicate messages are common. Interoperability gaps persist across health systems, making it harder to align patient records, including ADTs, across organizations. HIPAA compliance requirements add governance overhead for any team receiving or storing ADT data. How Metriport Uses ADT Data for Real-Time Patient Monitoring Metriport's ADT monitoring connects to feeds from Bamboo Health and state and regional HIEs , delivering real-time admission, discharge, and transfer notifications across the US healthcare system. What separates this from a standard alert feed is what happens immediately after the ADT fires: Metriport ties the alert to a Patient Encounter Bundle with the patient, encounter, and diagnosis data, and can trigger a network query to pull the discharge summary, medication list, and other transition documents into the patient's full longitudinal record. Because the alert is tied directly to the encounter data and can pull in the fuller record, care teams can act during an encounter instead of learning about the admission days later through a claims file. For value-based care organizations managing attributed populations, that window is where readmissions get prevented and transitional care management billing gets captured. FAQ What is an ADT feed in healthcare and how does it differ from an ADT database? An ADT feed is a real-time notification stream that pushes a message every time a patient is admitted, discharged, or transferred. An ADT database is a static record store built from those accumulated events over time; the feed tells you something just changed, while the database holds the full history of changes. What HL7 message types should I know for hospital ADT data? The seven message types that cover most real-world ADT traffic are A01 (admit), A02 (transfer), A03 (discharge), A04 (register), A08 (update demographics), A11 (cancel admit), and A13 (cancel discharge). The cancel events are frequently overlooked, but any system acting on an A01 or A03 needs to receive A11 and A13 messages or its records will drift out of sync. ADT alerts vs. claims data for tracking patient transitions: which is better for value-based care? ADT alerts give you real-time visibility into admissions and discharges, often within minutes of the event. Claims data arrives weeks or months later, long after the window to intervene has closed, making ADT the only practical signal for preventing readmissions and capturing transitional care management billing. How do I know if my organization meets the CMS ADT notification requirements? CMS requires most Medicare-participating hospitals to send ADT notifications to a patient's treating clinicians at the time of admission or registration, and immediately prior to or at the time of discharge or transfer, with non-compliance risking loss of Medicare and Medicaid participation. If your hospital lacks a reliable outbound ADT feed connected to primary care providers and care teams, you are likely out of compliance with the rule that took effect in 2021. Why does ADT data alone often fall short for care coordination? ADT messages capture movement events and a diagnosis code, but typically lack deeper clinical context like lab results, vitals, or care plans, which limits how actionable the alert is by itself. Connecting an ADT notification to a patient's full longitudinal record (including discharge summaries and medication lists) turns an alert into something a care team can actually act on.

title: Trellus vs Salesfinity: Best AI Cold Calling Tools 2026
summary: Compare Trellus.ai and Salesfinity for cold calling in 2026. Detailed feature analysis, pricing, and which AI dialer wins for SDR teams. Expert review.
body_text: ‍ Short Answer: Trellus.ai excels in real-time coaching and rep development with affordable pricing for individuals and small teams, while Salesfinity dominates high-volume dialing and enterprise collaboration. Choose Trellus.ai for conversational quality and personalized guidance; choose Salesfinity for maximum dial efficiency and advanced team features. Both are excellent—the right choice depends on whether your priority is rep development or pipeline velocity. For years, industry pundits have declared cold calling dead. Yet the reality tells a starkly different story. Despite the rise of digital marketing, email automation, and social selling, cold calling remains one of the most effective channels for B2B sales teams in 2026. The shift isn't about whether cold calling works—it's about how modern sales teams execute it. The evidence is compelling. According to recent market data, 82% of buyers remain open to meetings initiated through cold calls , demonstrating that decision-makers still value direct human contact. More impressively, cold calling drives 42% more growth when executed with proper strategy and preparation . These statistics underscore a fundamental truth: cold calling hasn't disappeared; instead, it has been transformed by artificial intelligence and sophisticated dialing technologies. This transformation is precisely why tools like Trellus.ai and Salesfinity have emerged as market leaders. Both platforms leverage AI to enhance what sales development representatives (SDRs) do best—having meaningful conversations with prospects. By automating administrative tasks, providing real-time coaching, and optimizing dialing efficiency, these platforms have made cold calling more productive than ever before. In this article, we'll conduct a detailed comparison of these two leading AI cold calling solutions to help you determine which platform best serves your team's needs. The Crowded AI Cold Calling Market: 173+ Tools and Counting The AI cold calling software market has exploded in recent years. According to G2, there are now over 173 AI-powered cold calling and sales enablement tools available to sales teams . This abundance of choice reflects both the market's recognition of cold calling's value and the intense competition among vendors to capture share in this growing segment. In such a crowded marketplace, becoming a market leader requires more than just basic functionality. Successful cold calling platforms must deliver on several critical capabilities. The must-have features for any credible AI cold calling solution include real-time call coaching that provides actionable guidance during live conversations, parallel dialing capabilities that enable reps to reach more prospects efficiently, seamless CRM integration that eliminates manual data entry, and AI-powered call transcription and analysis that creates institutional knowledge. Beyond these essentials, nice-to-have features differentiate market leaders from the rest. These include advanced objection handling powered by conversational AI, nurture automation that intelligently re-engages prospects at optimal times, team collaboration features like live call monitoring and coaching, comprehensive analytics dashboards that reveal performance trends, and compliance features that protect against regulatory violations. Key Takeaways from the Comparison For Real-Time Coaching Focus: Trellus.ai excels at providing live guidance during calls, making it ideal for teams that prioritize rep development and consistent messaging. The platform's AI coach listens to every call and delivers behavior suggestions in real-time, helping reps improve their conversational skills with each interaction. For Dialing Efficiency: Salesfinity's parallel dialing and contact enrichment capabilities make it the stronger choice for teams focused on maximizing dials per hour and connection rates. For Pricing Sensitivity: Trellus.ai offers more affordable entry points starting at $99.99/month for individuals, while Salesfinity's Silver plan begins at $200/user/month, making Trellus more accessible for smaller teams or solo SDRs exploring AI-powered cold calling. For Enterprise Features: Salesfinity's Enterprise plan includes dedicated customer success management, SSO/MFA, and advanced integrations like Gong and Slack, making it better suited for large organizations with complex requirements and multi-department workflows. Deep Dive into Trellus.ai Features: Why 8K+ SDRs Trust This Platform As the product owners of Trellus.ai, we're uniquely positioned to provide detailed insights into our platform's capabilities and evolution. Since our launch, we've onboarded more than 8,000 active users across diverse industries, and our platform maintains a 4.7-star rating on the Google Chrome Store . These metrics reflect not just adoption, but genuine user satisfaction and reliance on our platform for daily cold calling operations. Real-Time Call Coaching: Your AI Sales Coach on Every Call The cornerstone of Trellus.ai is our real-time call coaching engine. Unlike traditional sales coaching that happens after the call ends, our AI listens to every word of every conversation and provides live guidance to reps. This means when a rep is talking too fast, the AI suggests slowing down. When a rep is dominating the conversation, the AI prompts them to ask more questions. When a prospect raises an objection, the AI surfaces relevant counterarguments in real-time. This real-time intervention has proven transformative for sales teams. Reps report that the constant feedback loop accelerates their learning curve dramatically. New SDRs who might take months to develop conversational fluency can achieve competency in weeks with continuous AI coaching. The platform learns each rep's communication style and tailors suggestions accordingly, ensuring coaching feels personalized rather than robotic. The real-time coaching also creates consistency across your team. When every rep receives the same coaching on best practices, your entire team converges toward your organization's ideal sales methodology. This consistency translates directly to higher connection rates, more meetings booked, and shorter sales cycles. Objection Handling: AI-Powered Response Suggestions Objections are where most cold calls fall apart. A prospect says "we're not interested" or "we're locked into another vendor," and without a strong response, the call ends. Trellus.ai's objection handling system analyzes prospect statements in real-time and surfaces the most effective responses based on your team's historical win data and best practices. The system doesn't just suggest generic comebacks. Instead, it learns from your team's successful calls, identifying which objection responses lead to meetings booked or callbacks scheduled. Over time, the AI becomes increasingly intelligent about which responses work best for your specific industry, company size, and product type. This means your team's collective knowledge compounds, and newer reps benefit from the institutional wisdom of your top performers. The objection handling feature has been particularly valuable for new reps during their first 30-60 days. Rather than freezing when a prospect raises an objection, new reps can rely on AI suggestions to keep the conversation moving forward. This confidence boost accelerates ramp time and reduces early-career frustration. LinkedIn Superhuman Feature: Research and Personalization at Scale Cold calling without research is just noise. Trellus.ai's LinkedIn Superhuman feature transforms how reps prepare for calls. The tool automatically researches prospects on LinkedIn, identifying recent job changes, company announcements, content they've engaged with, and mutual connections. This research appears directly in the dialer interface, enabling reps to personalize their opening pitch in seconds. The efficiency gain is substantial. Rather than spending 5-10 minutes researching each prospect before dialing, reps have key talking points instantly available. This means more dials per hour, more personalized conversations, and higher connect rates. The feature integrates seamlessly with your existing sales engagement platform, whether that's Salesloft, Outreach, Apollo, or HubSpot. The LinkedIn Superhuman feature also reduces the friction of switching between tools. Reps don't need to open LinkedIn in a separate tab, search for the prospect, and then return to the dialer. Everything happens in one interface, keeping reps in flow state and maximizing their productivity. Parallel Dialing: Multi-Line Efficiency Without the Complexity Our Parallel plan enables reps to dial multiple numbers simultaneously, only connecting calls to the rep when a live person answers. This technology, borrowed from the telemarketing industry but refined for modern B2B sales, dramatically increases the number of meaningful conversations reps can have per day. Rather than waiting for each call to connect or ring out before dialing the next prospect, reps can have 3-5 calls in progress simultaneously. The platform's AI handles the initial connection and voicemail detection, passing only live conversations to the rep. This approach reduces wasted time on voicemails and disconnects while maintaining the personal touch that makes B2B cold calling effective. The parallel dialing feature is particularly valuable for teams working with large prospect lists or targeting high-volume markets. Reps can maintain their natural conversational style while dramatically increasing their throughput. The result is a significant boost in pipeline generation without requiring additional headcount. Conversational Intelligence and Call Analytics Every call on Trellus.ai is automatically transcribed and analyzed. The platform identifies key moments in the conversation—when objections were raised, when the prospect showed interest, when the rep asked effective questions. This conversational intelligence is then aggregated across your team to identify patterns. Sales managers can see which reps are booking the most meetings, which objections are most common, which opening statements resonate best, and which follow-up strategies convert prospects into opportunities. This data-driven approach to sales management replaces guesswork with evidence, enabling managers to coach reps on what actually works rather than what they think should work. The analytics dashboard also provides individual rep scorecards, showing each rep's performance against key metrics like connection rate, meeting booking rate, and average call duration. This transparency creates healthy accountability while also celebrating top performers and identifying reps who need additional support. Deep Dive into Salesfinity Features: A Balanced Perspective Salesfinity has earned its position as a market leader through relentless focus on dialing efficiency and team productivity. With 116 verified reviews on G2 and a 4.8-star rating , the platform has demonstrated consistent value delivery to its customer base. We recognize Salesfinity as a formidable competitor with genuine strengths that serve certain use cases exceptionally well. AI Parallel Dialer: 5.2x More Live Conversations Salesfinity's parallel dialing engine is engineered for maximum efficiency. The platform can simultaneously dial up to 5 numbers, intelligently routing live connections to available reps while automatically handling voicemails, disconnects, and invalid numbers. The result is a statistically significant increase in live conversations per rep per day. According to Salesfinity's case studies, teams using the parallel dialer achieve 5.2x more live conversations compared to traditional one-at-a-time dialing . For teams focused on volume and pipeline generation, this efficiency multiplier is transformative. The platform's AI voicemail detection has improved significantly, reducing the number of false positives that waste rep time. The parallel dialer also includes SmartRotate, which automatically rotates through your assigned phone numbers to maintain caller ID reputation and avoid spam flagging. This compliance-focused approach ensures your dialing remains effective even at high volumes. Nurture AI: Intelligent Follow-Up Automation One of Salesfinity's most innovative features is Nurture AI, which automatically analyzes call outcomes and schedules follow-ups at optimal times. When a prospect says "not now" or "call me back in three months," Nurture AI captures this intent and automatically schedules a callback at the precise moment when the prospect is most likely to be receptive. This automation eliminates the manual work of tracking follow-ups and ensures no opportunity slips through the cracks. For sales managers, it means their team's pipeline stays active without requiring constant manual intervention. The AI learns from your team's historical data to identify the best follow-up timing for different prospect segments and industries. Nurture AI also integrates with your CRM, automatically logging follow-up activities and updating prospect records. This creates a complete record of each prospect interaction, enabling managers to see the full lifecycle of each opportunity. Salesfloor: Team Collaboration and Live Coaching Salesfinity's Salesfloor feature brings remote teams together in a shared virtual space where managers can listen to live calls, provide whisper coaching, and create friendly competition through leaderboards and call challenges. This team-oriented approach to sales execution creates accountability and accelerates learning. The live coaching capability is particularly valuable for new rep onboarding. Rather than waiting for call recordings to review, managers can jump into live calls and guide reps in real-time. The competitive elements—leaderboards, call challenges, team goals—create engagement and motivation that traditional sales management approaches struggle to achieve. Salesfloor also enables peer learning. When top performers are on calls, other reps can listen in and learn from their techniques. This creates a culture of continuous improvement and knowledge sharing. SmartGenie: AI Web Research Integration Salesfinity's SmartGenie feature automatically researches prospects using web data, company announcements, and intent signals. The research appears directly in the dialer interface, enabling reps to personalize conversations without manual research time. This is similar in concept to Trellus's LinkedIn Superhuman feature but draws from a broader range of data sources. SmartGenie also identifies buying signals and intent indicators, helping reps prioritize their outreach toward prospects who are actively in-market for solutions like yours. This targeted approach improves connection quality and increases the likelihood of meaningful conversations. Contact List Enrichment: 6+ Data Providers Salesfinity integrates with six or more data providers to continuously enrich contact lists in real-time. Invalid numbers are replaced with current contact information, ensuring your dialing list stays fresh and accurate. This data enrichment is particularly valuable for teams working with older prospect lists or targeting hard-to-reach decision-makers. The platform's waterfall enrichment approach tries multiple data sources in sequence, maximizing the likelihood of finding valid contact information. For teams that rely on high-volume dialing, having accurate, current contact data is essential to achieving target dials per rep. Advanced Reporting and Analytics Salesfinity's reporting dashboard provides comprehensive visibility into team performance. Managers can see individual rep scorecards, team trends, call quality metrics, and pipeline impact. The analytics go beyond simple call counts to reveal which reps are booking meetings, which are advancing deals, and which need coaching support. The platform's integration with CRM systems ensures that call outcomes are automatically logged, creating a complete record of each prospect interaction. This eliminates manual CRM updates and ensures data accuracy. The 360° Rep Profiles feature provides detailed performance metrics for each rep, enabling data-driven coaching and performance management. Pricing Transparency: Trellus.ai vs Salesfinity (2026 Rates) Understanding the true cost of ownership is critical when evaluating sales tools. Both Trellus.ai and Salesfinity offer transparent, tiered pricing, but their approaches differ significantly. A single rep on Trellus's Parallel plan costs $149.99/month, compared to $200/month for Salesfinity's Silver plan. For a team of 10 reps, Trellus's Business plan (typically $1,500-2,000/month for 10 seats) compares favorably to Salesfinity's Gold plan at $2,990/month. However, Salesfinity's pricing includes more advanced features at lower tiers. The Gold plan's parallel dialer, Nurture AI, and SmartGenie are included at $299/month, whereas Trellus requires the Parallel plan ($149.99) plus a Business plan upgrade to access equivalent features. Both platforms report 4-month return on investment based on improved connect rates, meeting bookings, and reduced administrative time. The actual ROI depends heavily on your team's baseline performance and how effectively you implement the platform's features. For teams with 20+ reps, both platforms offer enterprise pricing that should be negotiated based on your specific requirements and usage patterns. Conclusion: Choosing the Right AI Cold Calling Platform The choice between Trellus.ai and Salesfinity ultimately depends on your team's primary objectives and constraints. Both platforms represent the state of the art in AI-powered cold calling, with strong user satisfaction, proven results, and continuous innovation. Choose Trellus.ai if your priorities are: •Real-time coaching and rep development •Affordable entry point for individuals or small teams •Seamless integration with your existing sales engagement platform •Focus on conversational quality over pure dial volume •Building institutional knowledge through conversational intelligence Choose Salesfinity if your priorities are: •Maximizing dials per rep and connection rates •Team collaboration and live coaching capabilities •Advanced contact enrichment and data quality •Comprehensive enterprise features and integrations •Nurture automation and intelligent follow-up scheduling The broader strategic insight is this: in 2026, cold calling success is no longer about dialing more numbers or having a better script. It's about leveraging AI to make every rep more effective, every conversation more personalized, and every team more data-driven. Whether you choose Trellus.ai or Salesfinity, you're investing in a platform that recognizes this reality and has built its product accordingly. The question isn't whether to use AI-powered cold calling tools—the market has clearly moved in that direction. The question is which platform aligns best with your team's culture, workflow, and growth objectives. Both Trellus.ai and Salesfinity are excellent choices; the right one for you depends on your specific needs, team size, and strategic priorities. Frequently Asked Questions 1. What is a Parallel Dialer? A parallel dialer is a technology that enables sales reps to dial multiple phone numbers simultaneously. Rather than waiting for each call to connect or ring out before dialing the next prospect, the dialer manages multiple calls in progress at once. When a live person answers, the call is routed to an available rep. Voicemails and disconnects are handled automatically. This approach significantly increases the number of meaningful conversations reps can have per day, often by 3-5x compared to traditional one-at-a-time dialing. Parallel dialers are particularly effective in high-volume sales environments where maximizing conversations per hour is critical to hitting pipeline targets. 2. How Does Trellus's Parallel Dialer Differ from Salesfinity's? Both platforms offer parallel dialing, but with different approaches and capabilities. Trellus's parallel dialer is designed to integrate directly into your existing sales engagement platform (Salesloft, Outreach, Apollo, etc.), providing a seamless experience within your current workflow. This integration-first approach means reps don't need to switch between tools. Salesfinity's parallel dialer is a more standalone feature that can dial up to 5 numbers simultaneously and includes advanced contact enrichment and voicemail detection. Trellus emphasizes integration and coaching, while Salesfinity emphasizes dialing efficiency and data quality. For teams already invested in a specific sales engagement platform, Trellus's approach may feel more natural. For teams looking for a comprehensive dialing solution, Salesfinity's feature set may be more compelling. 3. Why is Trellus.ai Better Suited for Professional B2B SaaS SDR Teams? Trellus.ai's real-time coaching engine and conversational intelligence are particularly valuable for B2B SaaS teams, where deal complexity and buyer sophistication require nuanced conversations. The platform's ability to provide real-time guidance during calls helps reps navigate complex objections and maintain consistent messaging. Additionally, Trellus's integration with modern sales engagement platforms makes it ideal for teams already using tools like Salesloft or Outreach, reducing implementation friction. The platform's focus on rep development and conversational quality aligns well with B2B SaaS sales culture, where building relationships and demonstrating expertise are critical to success. For teams where rep quality and consistency matter more than pure volume, Trellus.ai is the stronger choice. 4. Can Salesfinity and Trellus.ai Integrate with My CRM System? Yes, both platforms integrate with major CRM systems. Trellus.ai integrates with HubSpot, Salesforce, Outreach, Apollo, Amplemarket, and Zapier. Salesfinity integrates natively with HubSpot, Salesforce, Outreach, Salesloft, Amplemarket, and Apollo. Both platforms automatically log call outcomes, transcriptions, and summaries to your CRM, eliminating manual data entry and ensuring your pipeline stays accurate. If you're using a CRM system not listed above, contact each platform's support team to discuss custom integration options. Most modern CRM systems can be connected via API or webhook, so integration is usually possible even if not pre-built. 5. How Does AI Objection Analysis Enhance Sales Calls? AI objection analysis works by listening to prospect statements during calls and identifying common objection patterns. The AI then surfaces relevant counterarguments, case studies, or talking points that have proven effective in similar situations. This real-time guidance helps reps respond to objections more effectively without needing to think on their feet. Over time, the AI learns which responses work best for your specific industry and product, making suggestions increasingly accurate and relevant. This capability significantly improves close rates and reduces the number of calls lost to unhandled objections. For new reps, AI objection analysis provides a safety net that builds confidence and accelerates learning. For experienced reps, it provides data-driven insights that improve their already-strong skills.

body_text: SALT LAKE CITY — July 21, 2026 — ReposiTrak, Inc. (NYSE: TRAK), the leader in retail supply chain, compliance and traceability solutions, today announced that the first warehouse-delivered supplier is live with a major retailer on ReposiTrak SBT 2.0. The implementation marks a significant expansion of the Scan-based Trading model beyond its traditional use by Direct Store Delivery suppliers. Under the new program, the supplier ships products through the retailer’s warehouse and distribution network while retaining ownership of the inventory until each product is scanned and sold at the retail register. “Scan-based Trading is not limited to suppliers delivering directly to stores,” said Randy Fields, chairman and CEO of ReposiTrak. “This successful launch demonstrates that the financial and operational benefits of SBT can also be extended to warehouse-delivered products. The retailer does not have to purchase and finance the inventory before it sells, while the supplier gains direct visibility into store-level sales and inventory movement.” ReposiTrak SBT 2.0 uses point-of-sale activity as the data of record for invoicing and inventory ownership. When a participating product is scanned at the register, the transaction automatically triggers the transfer of ownership from the supplier to the retailer and supports accurate supplier payment. The model provides benefits to both trading partners. The retailer reduces its investment in inventory and aligns payment with actual consumer sales. The supplier maintains ownership until the product sells while gaining access to store-level sales and inventory information that can support better forecasting, replenishment and product availability. Optional ordering assistance is also available through ReposiTrak for suppliers or retailers that need additional support managing replenishment. Ordering recommendations can use sales and inventory data to identify store-level product needs, reduce out-of-stocks and improve inventory productivity. “The ability to support warehouse-delivered products substantially expands the addressable market for SBT,” Fields added. “Retailers and suppliers can now evaluate SBT based on the economics of the product category and the trading relationship—not simply on whether the supplier delivers directly to the store.” About ReposiTrak ReposiTrak, Inc. (NYSE: TRAK) is an AI-powered, integrated platform that connects retailers, wholesalers, suppliers, and food manufacturers through a suite of applications designed to reduce risk, support regulatory compliance, strengthen operational controls, and protect brand integrity. The ReposiTrak platform serves as a shared system of record across its solution areas, maintaining and synchronizing complex supplier and customer data to enable secure, accurate, and scalable information exchange. ReposiTrak’s solutions are organized into three core product families: traceability, compliance and risk management, and supply chain solutions. Through its scalable, cloud-based platform and U.S.-based team of experts, the Company helps organizations streamline operations, improve data transparency, and meet evolving regulatory requirements across the food supply chain. For more information, visit repositrak.com .
